title: Arista takes Ethernet into the rack, and the network becomes the backplane
key_facts: Arista Networks announced an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio for scale-up and scale-out AI networks, built with partners including AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft and Qualcomm.

The lead product, Etherlink SU-144, is an Ethernet-based scale-up architecture that connects up to 144 accelerators in one hop and up to 1,024 across racks, built on the ESUN (Ethernet for Scale-Up Networking) initiative.
Scale-out liquid-cooled rack reference designs come in 8-, 12- and 16-switch configurations built on 7060EX7 switches, each delivering 102.4 terabits per second.
Next-generation optics are said to raise rack capacity from 1.6 to 6.5 petabits per second and cut the data-centre footprint by nearly half.
Partners integrate and deliver the configured racks; Arista will show a fully assembled liquid-cooled rack at the Open Compute Project Global Summit, 12 to 15 Oct in San Jose.
Arista's Vijay Vusirikala says there is no near-term opportunity in Nvidia's proprietary scale-up links.
quote_evidence: In the AI era, the network can no longer be thought of as an independent pipe moving data between servers.
"There is no near-term opportunity because that is proprietary," Vusirikala told me.
A 16-switch rack configuration can involve 2,000 fibers, and on-site cabling invites bend-radius violations, miswiring, signal-integrity problems, and dead optics.
why_it_matters_hint: Arista is selling tested AI rack designs, not just switches, aimed at hyperscalers and AI cloud firms.
